What to look for in budget helmets

  • Fit first. The safest helmet is one that fits your head shape snugly with no pressure points — try several brands before buying.
  • Look for ECE 22.06. The current safety standard includes rotational-impact testing. A high SHARP star rating is a useful extra guide.
  • Pinlock-ready visor. Essential for the UK — a Pinlock insert stops fogging on cold, damp mornings.
  • Weight matters. Under ~1,600g keeps neck fatigue down on long days. Composite and carbon shells are lighter than polycarbonate.

Frequently asked questions

How much should I spend on budget helmets?

Our catalogue spans £67.49 to £149.99. Budget options under £150 cover the essentials, the £150–£400 mid-range hits the sweet spot for most UK tourers, and premium picks above £400 add refinement, lighter materials and longer-term durability.

Which brands are worth considering?

Popular, well-reviewed brands in this category include HJC, AGV, MT, Shark. All are stocked by SportsBikeShop with UK warranty support.

Are expensive helmets actually safer?

Not necessarily — every road-legal helmet meets the same ECE 22.06 standard. You pay more for lighter materials, lower noise, better ventilation and comfort features, not a higher safety floor. Always prioritise correct fit.

faq.a: Yes. Every helmet sold as road legal in the UK must meet the ECE 22.06 standard, so a £67.49 MT Targo S passes the same certified impact and rotational tests as a helmet costing hundreds more. Paying more buys lighter materials, lower noise and comfort features, not a higher safety floor. The most important factor at any price is a correct, snug fit.

faq.q: What do I give up by buying budget?
faq.a: Budget helmets typically use polycarbonate shells, which are a little heavier than the composite and carbon shells on premium lids, and they tend to be slightly noisier. You may also get simpler ventilation and less plush liners. That said, models like the HJC F70 and MT Thunder 4 SV include sun visors and Pinlock readiness that were once reserved for pricier helmets.

faq.q: Which budget helmet comes with a Pinlock?
faq.a: The MT Thunder 4 SV stands out because it ships with a Pinlock Max Vision anti-fog insert as standard, which is unusual under £150. A Pinlock is essential in the UK to stop your visor fogging on cold, wet mornings. Where a helmet is only Pinlock-ready, budget a little extra to add the insert separately.

faq.q: Do budget helmets have a sun visor?
faq.a: Many now do. The HJC F70, HJC i71, MT Thunder 4 SV and Shark Ridill 2 all feature a drop-down internal sun visor operated by a slider, so you can deal with low winter sun and bright glare without carrying sunglasses. It is one of the most useful features to look for when shopping at this price.

faq.q: How long will a budget helmet last?
faq.a: Build quality is good at this price, but as with any helmet the protective EPS liner ages. Replace it immediately after any significant impact, and otherwise plan on around five to seven years from first use as sweat, UV and wear degrade the materials. A budget helmet cared for properly will comfortably see out that lifespan.
